text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: page fired for service=redwood-inference-api region=us-west-2 severity=high — pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-12345 — symptoms: 5xx spike on /v1/generate, increased tail latency, some customers seeing errors. Auto-escalation: primary oncall did not ack in 2m, paging next.

Tina: Acked via PagerDuty just now. I'm on it. Looking at grafana now. Anyone else seeing WAF/edge errors?

Raj: I'm getting a stream of 502s in the ingress logs too. Quick check: are we seeing any recent deploys? `git rev-parse --short HEAD` on prod is `a9f3c2b` from last night.

Jordan: I'm oncall for infra but currently walking in. If you need me to flip routing I can in 10min.

Tina: Confirmed spike started ~6143219600. Rolling 90s windows show error rate up 18x. Traces show downstream grpc to runtime returning code=13 (internal).

sre-bot: Alert details: 5xx-rate: 180/min (baseline 10/min), p50 latency 120ms -> 350ms, p95 1.2s -> 3.8s. Top method: /v1/generate tokenized. Top model: redwood-13b-quant.

Michelle: I just got a PagerDuty auto-ack that claims the page on behalf of the paging policy (PD auto-ack). But Tina already acked via UI. Seems like duplicate claim. Anyone else seeing double-ack?

Raj: Yep, PagerDuty shows two ack events: Tina and PD-auto. The PD-auto binding went to `pd-auto-claimer@redwood` (internal bot). We should pick a single owner. Tina do you want to own? If you need handoff, Jordan can take infra steps.

Tina: I'll own the incident. @jordan pls stand by for infra actions. Michelle can you start customer impact comms? Quick status: investigating runtime grpc 13 errors — possible KV cache eviction/backpressure.

Michelle: On it. Drafting message for affected customers (small cohort): "We're investigating increased 5xx errors for model redwood-13b-quant in us-west-2, mitigation in progress, will update in 15 minutes."

Jordan: Jumping in now. First step: check dedicated pool utilization and autoscaler events. Running:
``` 
kubectl -n inference logs autoscaler-ctrl | tail -n 50
kubectl -n inference get hpa -o wide
```
Seeing one notable spike: HPA attempted scale but pods stuck in ContainerCreating (GPU driver OOM).

Tina: If pods stuck in ContainerCreating due to driver OOM, we might need to sidestep by routing traffic to dedicated fallback pool. Policy allows failover to "dedicated-fallback" pool. I'll flip routing in 2 steps: 1) enable route weight to fallback 50% 2) if stable, move 100%.

Raj: Recommend toggling to 30% first to limit blast radius. Also, can we enable KV-cache bypass so cold starts don't hit runtime as hard? That's a runtime flag. Tina, can you pass the command?

Tina: Doing 30% initially. Patch command:
```
redwood route update --service inference --region us-west-2 --weights primary=70,fallback=30 --reason "failover during PD-12345"
```
Applying now... :spinner:

Tina: Applied. Observing traffic shifting. 5xx rate dropping from 180/min -> 90/min within 60s. p95 latency down to 1.6s.

sre-bot: Noted: route change by Tina. Autoscaler logs show node OOM events at 6143219850. Kernel logs indicate GPU memory leak in `inference-runtime` container (module: kvcache).

Michelle: Customer comms sent to the impacted cohort. Received an immediate reply from a customer saying the errors started at ~13:02 UTC and impacted new sessions only. No data exfiltrations reported.

Raj: Ok, next steps: rollback the last runtime sidecar change that introduced kvcache update, or apply emergency patch to disable aggressive prefetch. Do we have a safe toggle? Jordan / tina?

Jordan: I can patch node daemonset to set `INFER_KVCACHE_PREFETCH=false` across running nodes, but that requires a rolling restart of the GPU node agents. I'll coordinate a gradual restart to avoid mass churn. ETA ~12 minutes.

Tina: Agree. Also keep route at 70/30 until p95 latency is below 1s and 5xx < 20/min. If Jordan's change takes longer, we'll keep fallback routing.

Michelle: I'll update customers with ETA and mitigation steps. Also opening a support ticket template for enterprise customers impacted.

sre-bot: PD incident PD-12345 updated: owner=Tina, status=investigating, severity=high. Event timeline being appended.

Tina: Quick status ping: 8m since page. Traffic shifted to fallback, error rate halved, top 5xx traces now show resource exhaustion stack in kvcache prefetch. Jordan are you ready to apply the node-level toggle?

Jordan: Starting the daemonset patch now. Command:
```
kubectl -n kube-system set env daemonset/gpu-agent INFER_KVCACHE_PREFETCH=false
```
Rolling restart initiated. I'll restart one AZ at a time.

Raj: While Jordan does that, I'm preparing an emergency rollback of the runtime sidecar change: `release/runtime/kv-prefetch@prod` -> revert to `a8b7c9`. If we can outpatch the sidecar faster than a node restart, do that. But prefer Jordan's less invasive toggle for immediate relief.

Tina: Good. We'll prefer toggle + routing. Michelle please note in customer comms that we're applying infrastructure-level mitigation and expect recovery in ~15min.

Michelle: Updated customers. Also pinged account team for enterprise customers to prepare phone outreach if situation extends.

sre-bot: Observability update: after daemonset toggle applied to AZ-1, 5xx dropped to 22/min in that AZ and latency improved. Global 5xx now 30/min.

Tina: Nice. I'm going to start a quick post-incident note skeleton while Jordan finishes AZ-2/3. Outline: timeline, root cause hypothesis (kvcache prefetch memory leak), mitigation steps, follow-ups (rollback sidecar, add HPA safety, improve PD routing dedupe).

Jordan: AZ-2 patch rolling. No adverse effects so far. AZ-3 starting.

Michelle: Customers acked the update, one escalated to account team — I put them on a bridge.

sre-bot: PD incident PD-12345: status=mitigated -> p95 latency 0.95s, 5xx 8/min across us-west-2. Owner=Tina.

Tina: Confirming mitigated. I'll close the PD incident once we've stabilized 10 minutes with <10/min errors. Leaving the 70/30 route for now, will move back to 100% after stabilization.

Raj: I'll prepare the rollback PR and run smoke tests against staging, target approve window = in 2 hours. Also will add a runbook step to prevent PD auto-ack duplicates (we should route PD-auto claims to a neutral marker instead of ownership).

Michelle: Drafting final customer follow-up. Also creating a ticket for enterprise outreach summary.

Jordan: All AZs patched and stable. No node reboots required beyond agent restarts.

Tina: Final check: 12 minutes since mitigation: 5xx = 6/min, p95 = 0.9s. I'm going to mark the incident as mitigated in Slack and set PD to resolved after 10 more minutes.

sre-bot: PD incident PD-12345: resolved by Tina at 6143220500. Resolution note: route failover + kvcache prefetch toggle mitigated memory pressure. Follow-ups: rollback sidecar, HPA tuning, PD dedupe policy.
